races.title: State Senate, District 24
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Danny Earl Britt, Jr.
cands.bio: Republican attorney from Lumberton and North Carolina state senator, first elected in 2016 and serving since 2017. Former assistant district attorney in the Robeson County DA's office and private-practice lawyer. Lieutenant Colonel in the North Carolina Army National Guard as of 2022.
cands.gaps: We could not find where he grew up or when he settled in Lumberton. We found no statements from him on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no documented actions by him on those issues in the pages we could read, and no endorsements for 2026. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. His 2018 survey named education, jobs and law enforcement as priorities, with no specific positions. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia says he was born in Robeson County and lives in Lumberton; it does not say where he grew up, and the dated record only shows him in North Carolina as an adult from his 2016 Senate run onward (about 10 years), though he also worked as a Robeson County prosecutor.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the North Carolina State Senate since 2017, after working as a private-practice attorney and as an assistant district attorney in Robeson County. Earned a J.D. in 2003 and holds a Lieutenant Colonel rank in the Army National Guard.
qual.why: Nine years of prior legislative service plus a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee chair posts were not counted.
qual.label: Nine years of prior legislative service plus a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee chair posts were not counted.

cands.name: Catina Hamm
cands.bio: Catina Hamm is the Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 24 in 2026, facing incumbent Republican Danny Earl Britt. Her Democratic primary was canceled, so she advanced to the general election. The sources I had list no jobs or offices held.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from Sway voting groups: Better Future NC (Cam Pruette), Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Imani's Pix, Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress (Vote for Peace), Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and Waves of Democracy. These are voter-guide groups, not major organizations.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Catina Hamm was born or raised, when she came to North Carolina, or her work history and any offices held. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we found no campaign platform, interviews or questionnaires. We found no public statements from her on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, education, policing or land ownership, and no actions in office to report. We found no controversies or foreign ties, but the sources we had were thin.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No work history or offices held could be found in the sources available.
qual.why: Her background could not be established, so no score is given.
